# Dilemma v3.7.1

Scheduled and random quizzes now share question history on each server, so a fact used in a random can be considered when generating a later saved-topic quiz and vice versa.

- Preserve the 365-question history of each saved topic and the 1460-random history window. Also compare against the latest 365 scheduled questions across the server, including retained questions from removed topics. Keep servers isolated.
- Give generation at most 20 recent/relevant questions instead of selecting the oldest end of descending history. Promote rejected questions on retry.
- Reject normalized exact repeats locally. Short-list at most five possible related facts using question and answer terms, including inflected names, and review only those cases with the existing AI model. Allow different facts about the same subject.
- Bound each semantic review to short references, a strict boolean response, 512 output tokens and the existing request queue and overall generation deadline. Reject invalid, refused, incomplete or unavailable reviews before publication and release unused quiz reservations.
- Read bounded history once per publication with parallel queries. Fetch explanations only for possible matches and add the saved-topic history index.
- Serialize publication per server within the bot process through the final save, so concurrent publications can see each other's stored questions.
- Add isolated tests for cross-mode history, paraphrase handling, reversed questions, recent prompt order, inflected names, failure recovery, parallel publication, history boundaries and query limits. Automated AI checks use simulated responses.

Apply the additive `20261104090000_shared_question_history_index` migration before starting this version. The migration adds an index and preserves quiz history and balances. No Discord command registration or player-guide text change is required when upgrading from v3.7.0.

Semantic coverage remains bounded by retained history, candidate selection and model accuracy. The per-server publication queue covers one bot process; multiple replicas would need a shared publication lock.
